posts.content: CVE-2026-84448 libheif: heap over-read via inline mask data in heif_region functions, fixed in 1.23.2. CVSS 4.0. Update libheif now. #CVE #infosec #libheif https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-84448/

CVE-2026-84448.description: libheif is a HEIF and AVIF file format decoder and encoder. Prior to 1.23.2, the public heif_region_item_add_region_inline_mask_data() function in libheif/api/libheif/heif_regions.cc accepts mask_data_len without verifying that it equals the byte count required by width and height. A later heif_region_get_mask_image() call derives the read length from the region geometry, so an undersized stored buffer causes heif_region_get_inline_mask_image() to read beyond the heap allocation and copy adjacent bytes into the returned monochrome mask image. This can disclose heap data or crash an application that constructs region metadata through the writer API, while the file-parsing path is not affected because it validates the canonical mask size. This issue is fixed in version 1.23.2.

posts.content:
Upload2Shell · CVE-2026-125396 · pwn.ai research

https://pwn.ai/upload2shell

🚨 BREAKING: SECURITY RESEARCHERS FOUND A VULNERABILITY THAT CAN TURN A SIMPLE FILE UPLOAD INTO REMOTE CODE EXECUTION ACROSS MULTIPLE MAJOR PLATFORMS.

Dubbed Upload2Shell (CVE-2026-125396), the flaw affects Ghostscript, a widely used document-processing tool sitting behind everything from WordPress uploads and email previews to Linux printing services.

Researchers at pwnai demonstrated how malicious files could escape Ghostscript's -dSAFER sandbox and execute commands on vulnerable servers. They confirmed working attack paths involving Debian 13, WordPress, Roundcube, MediaWiki and several popular WordPress plugins. Their research also reached Google's production document-processing infrastructure.

Here's the scary part: attackers don't necessarily need to upload an obvious executable. A seemingly harmless image or PDF can reach Ghostscript through ImageMagick, triggering the vulnerable interpreter during routine processing. In one Roundcube test, simply viewing an email caused a malicious attachment to be processed. No attachment click was needed.

The flaw affects Ghostscript versions before 10.08.0, although patched distribution packages are also available. Not every installation is exposed, and there's no confirmed widespread exploitation in the wild. One vulnerable component. Multiple applications. Completely different ways to reach it.

Full technical breakdown, affected software, exploit chain and patches ↓
https://thecybersecguru.com/exploits/upload2shell-ghostscript-rce-cve-2026-125396/

#Upload2Shell #Ghostscript #WordPress #Linux #CyberSecurity

posts.content: CVE-2026-84449 libheif: integer overflow in RGB to YCbCr conversion can read out of bounds on huge images. CVSS 3.7, low severity. Fixed in 1.19.6, so update when you can. #CVE #infosec #libheif https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-84449/

CVE-2026-84449.description: libheif is a HEIF and AVIF file format decoder and encoder. Prior to 1.19.6, Op_RGB24_32_to_YCbCr::convert_colorspace() stores image-plane strides in an integer width that can overflow for extremely large RGB images created through heif_image_create() and heif_image_add_plane(). The resulting wrapped stride causes the conversion loop in libheif/color-conversion/rgb2yuv.cc to compute an invalid input pointer and read beyond the allocated interleaved plane while heif_context_encode_image() performs RGB-to-YCbCr conversion. This can crash the encoding process. This issue is fixed in version 1.19.6.

This is due to a byte-level denylist on the `tpgb_acf_key[]` and `tpgb_acf[]` parameters that fails to block Unicode look-alike characters — such as U+1E87 and U+00E7 in a key like `ẇp_çapabilities` — whose UTF-8 byte sequences do not match any ASCII-based pattern check, while the database's default accent-insensitive collation (`utf8mb4_unicode_ci` / `utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci`) treats the decorated key as equivalent to the canonical `wp_capabilities` row, causing `update_user_meta()` to overwrite the newly registered user's role with `administrator`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to register a new account bearing the full Administrator role, gaining complete control over the WordPress site including the ability to install plugins, modify files, and execute arbitrary code. The nonce required by the handler is publicly emitted on any page containing the tp-login-register block, making the full exploit chain — nonce retrieval, a single crafted registration POST, and the plugin's own `autologin` flow — trivially reachable on any default install where user registration is enabled. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

CVE-2026-114495.description: codebase-memory-mcp provides local code intelligence for developers and AI agents through a persistent graph and MCP tools. Prior to 0.9.0, automatic import of a repository's .codebase-memory/ artifact allocated a decompression buffer using the attacker-controlled 64-bit original_size value from artifact.json but truncated that value to int when passing the destination capacity to the Zstandard decompressor. A value with bit 31 set became negative and was sign-extended to a large size_t, allowing the decompressor to write frame content beyond the actual allocation. Indexing a malicious repository containing the crafted artifact could corrupt heap memory with attacker-controlled bytes, causing a reliable crash and potentially code execution. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.
